analysis.title: US Conviction List - Directors' Cut: October 2026 Update
key_insights: The October update adds Amazon (AMZN), Burlington Stores (BURL), Huntington Ingalls (HII), Johnson Controls (JCI) and Occidental Petroleum (OXY). It removes Air Products (APD), ConocoPhillips (COP), Golar LNG (GLNG), Loar Holdings (LOAR) and Tyson Foods (TSN). The removed names remain Buy-rated, and list membership is not a rating change.

The list holds 23 Buy-rated US stocks. Median upside to price target is 39% and median FY2 revenue growth is 9%. Median beta is 1.1. 91% of names have upside to the FY2 consensus metric, and 22% have a Street Buy share of 50% or less.
Top upside to price target on the list: NXT 81%, HII 64%, TPG 54%, AMZN 51%, DASH 50%. Largest upside to consensus FY2 EPS: HII 11%, TPG 10%, DAL 9%, AMZN 8%, VRTX 7%.

List performance in September was weak. CLS led at +20.7%, then AMAT +11.6% and DAL +7.0%. DASH (-20.8%), TPG (-18.5%) and CWST (-12.9%) lagged. The S&P 500 fell 0.3%, the equal-weight index fell 4.8% and GS Americas coverage fell 5.9%.
Hit rate since inception (n = 130) is 42% vs the S&P 500 and 47% vs the equal-weight index. Over the trailing twelve months it is 34% and 38%. In September it was 17% and 26%.

Fed pivot: the Fed raised rates in September with near-unanimous support, and its projections keep rates elevated through 2029. GS forecasts only one more hike, in December. It argues core PCE inflation is running 40bp below Fed expectations and oil is receding. Rates are at levels not seen since before the 2008 financial crisis.

GS lists six market pivot points: rates, AI, energy, Congress, competition for capital, and China. Wilson and Trivedi see rates, energy and AI as the three biggest risks, but say they are well priced, so risk relief is more likely than escalation in October.

AI trade is rotating from infrastructure to applications. GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN treaded water in September. META was the strongest trillion-dollar stock, helped by its Muse AI product. Semis and security software rose, while most enterprise software did not.

Oil: Persian Gulf oil shipments are back to pre-war levels per Yulia Grigsby, so GS says something else is lifting prices. Supply disruption is most acute in natural gas, diesel and jet fuel because of damaged LNG facilities and refineries and blocked trade routes. Europe is most exposed through LNG.
Midterms: prediction markets imply Democrats win the Senate with over 60% odds and the House with over 90%. GS notes that Democratic generic-ballot odds have moved with gasoline prices this year.

AMZN (PT $375): AWS grew 37% in the June quarter with a 39% operating margin. Chips and AI businesses each run at a $25b annual revenue rate. Backlog is $496b, up 154% y/y. Capex guidance was raised 10% to $220bn on component inflation. GS is about 2%/6% above the Street on 2026/2027 AWS revenue and about 130bps above on 2028 North America EBIT margin.

BURL (PT $382): GS expects 10%+ revenue growth through 2028 from 3%+ same-store sales and at least 110 net new stores a year, toward 1,500 stores by end-2028. Ex tariff refunds, 2Q operating margin rose about 100bps on a 2% comp. Concerns about warm weather and freight costs are called overdone. GS FY27/FY28 EPS is about 1% above consensus.

HII (PT $439): re-added after a March removal and a margin-driven pullback. Shipbuilding revenue grew 15-20% for four straight quarters on a $32.7bn backlog. GS expects margins to improve on submarine contract terms at 3Q26 results. HII trades at 9.0x CY27E EV/EBITDA vs 12.0x for large-cap defense peers.

JCI (PT $191): organic growth accelerated to +10% in F3Q26 from +4% a year earlier. Organic orders have grown over 30% for three quarters and backlog is a record $21bn. GS forecasts FY27 organic growth of +11% vs +8.7% consensus. Data centers are projected to rise from 12% of revenue in 2025 to about 33% by 2029. GS expects EPS to more than double through 2028 under new CEO Joakim Weidemanis.

OXY (PT $69): GS upgraded OXY to Buy on Sep 30. Advanced recovery could add 2 BBOE of reserves. A $4bn cash cost-cutting plan is under way, and GS models $3.4bn of it. Principal debt is down 60% to about $11.8bn against a $10bn target. GS sees excess cash going to dividend growth, up to $4.00/share in an upside case, or buybacks.

Stocks vs bonds: GS strategist Ben Snider says US bubble fears are overdone because the S&P 500 P/E has compressed by 3 turns this year. Peter Oppenheimer flags rising capital demand from deficits and the AI build-out as competition for stock and bond investors.

China: policymakers announced targeted fiscal and monetary easing on Sep 29. Hui Shan expects RMB appreciation and export-rebate cuts to manage trade surpluses and trade tensions. Xinquan Chen sees a modest growth impulse.

earnings_insights: Option-implied earnings-day moves vs the 8-quarter average actual move: DAL 10/9 implied 6% vs 7% actual avg. WFC 10/13 4% vs 5%. UNH 10/13 6% vs 9%. CFG 10/16 3% vs 3%. ORLY 10/22 5% vs 3%. NXT 10/23 13% vs 14%. UPS 10/27 6% vs 6%. CLS 10/29 11% vs 12%. MSFT 10/29 5% vs 7%. CSL 10/29 6% vs 8%. TPG 10/29 0% vs 4%. CWST 10/30 0% vs 4%. AMZN 10/30 6% vs 6%. HII 10/30 10% vs 12%.

AMZN June quarter results (reported): AWS revenue growth +37%, AWS operating margin 39%, advertising revenue +26% y/y. 2026 capex guidance raised 10% in July to $220bn. AMZN Q3 results are expected 10/30.

BURL: excluding tariff refunds, 2Q (reported) operating margin expanded about 100bps on a 2% comp. 3Q results are the next catalyst, with focus on fall comps, weather sensitivity, Home trends and whether reinvested tariff refunds lift sales.
HII: 3Q26 results are expected 10/31 per the analyst write-up (the options table shows 10/30). GS expects margin improvement on submarine contract terms and conservative medium-term guidance.

JCI: GS expects an F4Q26 EPS beat vs consensus (GS estimate, not yet reported) and an FY2027 organic growth guide above the +8.7% consensus. F3Q26 (reported) organic growth was +10% vs +4% a year earlier, with organic order growth over 30% for three quarters.
CLS: Mike Ng expects a constructive 3Q result later in October and an analyst day. Since Sep 1, GS cut its CLS FY2 EPS estimate 7% and price target 5%.

OXY: catalysts are execution on the $4bn cash flow plan, progress to the under-$10bn principal debt target, return of capital, formal 2027 capex guidance against a roughly $5.9bn starting point, and quarterly production and free cash flow.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in September, with almost the entire committee in support
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed moved from accommodative to restrictive. The move was described as removing a dose of accommodation. Projections keep rates elevated through 2029.

macro_indicators.reading: GS forecasts one more hike, in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects the FOMC to conclude further hikes are unnecessary as inflation and oil recede. It argues markets are pricing too many hikes.
Lower-than-projected inflation is the basis for GS pushing back on further Fed hikes.
Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats. Odds have moved with gasoline prices.

macro_indicators.reading: More than 90% chance Democrats net at least 3 seats
macro_indicators.interpretation: A divided Congress is the market-implied base case.

risk_factors: Rates, energy and AI are the three biggest market risks per Wilson and Trivedi, though GS says they are well priced.
Persistent oil, nat gas, diesel and jet fuel supply disruption feeding inflation and rates.
AMZN: competition, failure to scale high-margin businesses, investment headwinds to margin, regulatory changes and macro volatility.
BURL: execution, higher markdowns, freight and wage costs, low-income consumer pressure and competition. Warm fall weather could hurt seasonal sales.
HII: geopolitics, Department of War spending priorities and margins.
JCI: data center demand slowing, productivity initiatives falling short and execution missteps.
OXY: commodity prices, shareholder return priorities and cash flow improvement execution.
Private credit concerns and fund redemptions are weighing on alternative asset managers such as TPG.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots gasoline prices against the Democratic generic ballot, and the text says the two have moved together this year.
Exhibit 13 shows HII Shipbuilding adjusted EBIT margin with a +360bps expansion annotation.
Exhibit 12 shows HII Shipbuilding revenue with a +8.5% CAGR annotation.
Exhibit 14 shows JCI organic revenue growth against organic order growth, with orders above 30% for three straight quarters.
Exhibit 15 shows OXY free cash flow and reinvestment rate, with GS forecasting a sustainably lower reinvestment rate.
Exhibit 16 bridges OXY 2025 adjusted FCF to GSe 2030 adjusted FCF at $65/bbl WTI, showing about $3.4bn of cash flow improvement.
vol_and_positioning: Option-implied earnings moves for list names are in line with or below the 8-quarter average actual move for most names. The widest gaps are TPG and CWST (0% implied vs 4% actual) and UNH (6% vs 9%). ORLY is the only name implying more than history (5% vs 3%).
Most volatile expected prints: NXT 13% implied, CLS 11% and HII 10%.
22% of list names have a Street Buy share of 50% or less. HII (50%), CSL (50%), UPS (48%), EL (47%) and OXY (37%) have the lowest Street Buy shares.
Alternative asset managers sold off in September on rising rates, private credit concerns and selective fund redemptions. Transportation stocks sold off on consumer and jet fuel exposure.
The S&P 500 P/E multiple has compressed by 3 turns this year while US stocks held steady in September and bonds kept falling.
geopolitical: US-Iran War remains unresolved and is contributing to higher oil prices, inflation and rates globally.
Russia-Ukraine war remains unresolved, also contributing to higher oil prices, inflation and rates.

Persian Gulf oil exports are back at pre-war levels per Yulia Grigsby, so other factors are lifting oil. Damage to LNG facilities and refineries and blocked trade routes hit nat gas, diesel and jet fuel supply.
Europe is most exposed to the LNG supply disruption.
US midterm elections loom, with prediction markets favoring Democratic majorities in both chambers.
China announced targeted fiscal and monetary easing on September 29. Rising trade tensions and large trade surpluses may lead to RMB appreciation and export-rebate cuts.

tension_points.bull_case: Ben Snider says fears that US stocks are in a bubble are overdone, because the S&P 500 P/E has compressed by 3 turns this year while earnings are the key support.
tension_points.bear_case: Peter Oppenheimer notes demand for capital from the private and public sectors is rising with large fiscal deficits and the AI build-out, which competes with equities. Bond prices kept falling in September.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Corporate earnings are the key to watch, and weak earnings would undercut the case against a bubble.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects only one more hike, in December, as core PCE runs 40bp below Fed projections and oil prices recede, so risk relief is more likely than escalation.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets have priced a string of further hikes, and the Fed's projections keep rates elevated through 2029 at levels not seen since before 2008.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core PCE inflation stops running below Fed expectations or oil prices stop receding, which would keep further hikes on the table.
